summary: Host-only authenticator cache can forward credentials across services on the same host
description:
Researcher: Francesco Sabiu

## Summary

ORT's `OrtAuthenticator` caches server credentials by `requestingHost` only. The cache key omits scheme, port, realm, and URL scope, so credentials resolved for one service can be reused for a different service on the same hostname.

In a local proof, credentials learned for:

```text
https://scott:tiger@www.example.com:8443/private
```

are later returned for:

```text
https://www.example.com:9443/attacker
```

The second service is on a different port and did not provide those credentials.

## Affected code

Reviewed commit: `5a6ffa61f3f6f86e0b0fa8a8747a6d94924b8ea5`

Relevant file: `utils/ort/src/main/kotlin/OrtAuthenticator.kt`

The implementation declares:

```kotlin
private val serverAuthentication: ConcurrentHashMap<String, PasswordAuthentication> = ConcurrentHashMap()
```

and retrieves / stores credentials with:

```kotlin
serverAuthentication[requestingHost]?.let { return it }
...
serverAuthentication[requestingHost] = it
```

The HTTP client can use this authenticator reactively for 401 responses, and can also add Basic `Authorization` preemptively when `OkHttpClientHelper.enablePreemptiveAuthentication` is enabled.

## Local proof

I added a focused unit test to ORT's existing `OrtAuthenticatorTest`:

```kotlin
"Cached credentials are reused across different ports on the same host" {
    val host = "www.example.com"
    val url1 = "https://scott:tiger@$host:8443/private"
    val url2 = "https://$host:9443/attacker"

    val authenticator = OrtAuthenticator()
    authenticator.requestPasswordAuthentication(url1, 8443) shouldNot beNull()

    authenticator.requestPasswordAuthentication(url2, 9443) shouldNotBeNull {
        userName shouldBe "scott"
        String(password) shouldBe "tiger"
    }
}
```

Command:

```sh
JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@17 PATH=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@17/bin:$PATH ./gradlew --no-daemon :utils:ort:test --tests org.ossreviewtoolkit.utils.ort.OrtAuthenticatorTest --rerun-tasks
```

Observed result:

```text
OrtAuthenticatorTest > Cached credentials are reused across different ports on the same host STARTED
OrtAuthenticatorTest > Cached credentials are reused across different ports on the same host PASSED

BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 48s
```

## Impact

ORT analyzes package manifests, lockfiles, source artifacts, VCS URLs, SPDX external document references, and scanner inputs that can cause outbound HTTP or VCS fetches. If one fetch resolves credentials for `host:portA`, a later attacker-controlled dependency/source URL on `host:portB` can trigger authentication and receive cached credentials for the first service.

This is a credential-forwarding / confused-deputy issue. The attacker does not need access to the protected service; they need control over a dependency/source URL that ORT will fetch after credentials have been cached for the same hostname.

I am conservatively rating this Moderate because exploitation depends on fetch ordering and same-host different-service placement. Suggested CVSS v3.1: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N`.

## Duplicate review

I searched public GitHub issues/advisories for the host-only authenticator-cache issue. I found two related but non-duplicate PRs:

- `#10636`: passes the full URL to the authenticator so credential lookup has more context.
- `#4315`: synchronizes JGit authentication with ORT's authenticator.

Those do not describe or fix the host-only `serverAuthentication[requestingHost]` cache key in `OrtAuthenticator`.

## Safety

The proof is fully local and uses synthetic URLs with ORT's own unit-test harness. I did not test any live third-party service, registry, repository, account, or credential.

## Suggested fix

Key the server authentication cache by an origin-safe tuple, not only hostname. At minimum include scheme, host, and effective port. If available, include authentication realm or normalized URL scope, and avoid reusing URL-userinfo credentials across different origins.
